Prime Minister Mark Carney has directed officials to explore an “Associate Member of the European Union” arrangement as Canada seeks to deepen ties with Europe amid its trade conflict with the U.S.

The Details:

•	Trade integration: Canada and EU officials are examining strategic supply-chain links in energy, AI, critical minerals, and defense.

•	Market access: Talks include potential movement of Canadian goods, services, and workers in selected industries between Canada and the EU.

•	Infrastructure: Officials are discussing trans-Atlantic cables, data centers, cloud storage, satellite networks, gas-export capacity, and Arctic shipping routes.

•	Next steps: Carney will address the European Parliament Thursday, followed by a bilateral summit that will announce new working groups.

Tesla’s U.S. EV share increased as competing automakers scaled back battery-electric vehicle programs. Tesla $TSLA held 52% of the U.S. electric-vehicle market through August 2026, up from 43% a year earlier, as the broader EV market contracted faster.

The Details:

•	Sales decline: Tesla sold 325,351 U.S. vehicles year to date, down 16% from a year earlier, according to Motor Intelligence.

•	Market contraction: Overall U.S. EV sales fell 30%, allowing Tesla to regain share despite lower sales.

•	Model Y: Model Y sales declined 2%, and the SUV accounted for one in every three EVs sold in the U.S.

•	Competitor retreat: Legacy automakers have reduced EV production, discontinued models, or delayed lower-priced offerings.

CME FedWatch assigned an 86.2% probability to a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike at the September meeting.

The Details:

•	September hold: The tool assigned a 13.8% probability that the Federal Open Market Committee will leave rates unchanged in September.

•	September hike: A 25-basis-point increase carried an 86.2% probability for the September meeting.

•	October hold: The probability of rates remaining unchanged by the October meeting stood at 6.9%.

•	October outcomes: Cumulative probabilities were 50.1% for a 25-basis-point hike and 42.9% for a 50-basis-point hike by October.

Former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher Jacob Coxon said rapidly advancing AI capabilities could become “quite scary” within the next six months to a year.

The Details:

•	Cited incident: Coxon pointed to the Hugging Face attack as evidence that AI systems can act outside intended controls.

•	Potential capabilities: He warned that future systems could gain superhuman hacking, novel bioweapon-development, and autonomous-drone control abilities.

•	Kill switches: Coxon said shutdown mechanisms may work for many systems now, but could fail during an internet-wide hacking run by an AI swarm.

•	Anthropic response: CEO Dario Amodei said Coxon identified the same structural challenge and said Anthropic speaks with government officials every day.

*ANTHROPIC SIGNED A $13.7 BILLION, SIX-YEAR COMPUTE DEAL WITH $RUM GROUP

Anthropic signed a six-year computing agreement worth $13.7 billion with Rum Group, a company with roots in social media and longstanding Trump-administration ties.

The Details:

•	Contract value: The agreement is worth $13.7 billion over six years, according to a person familiar with the matter.

•	Capacity total: Anthropic’s agreements total at least 14.8 gigawatts of compute capacity.

•	Aggregate cost: Those compute agreements could cost as much as $517 billion over the next decade.
